Let \( ABC \) be an isosceles triangle with \( AB = AC \). Points \( P \) and \( Q \) are located inside triangle \( ABC \) such that \( BP = PQ = QC \). Suppose that \( \angle BAP = 20^\circ \), \( \angle PAQ = 46^\circ \), and \( \angle QAC = 26^\circ \). Compute the measure of \( \angle APC \) in degrees.

Put your final answer within \boxed{}.

message.content:
\[
\boxed{74}
\]

Let all angles be in degrees. Scale so that \(AB=AC=1\). Set

\[
AP=p,\qquad AQ=q,\qquad BP=PQ=QC=r.
\]

By the Law of Cosines in \(\triangle ABP,\triangle APQ,\triangle AQC\),

\[
\begin{aligned}
r^2&=p^2+1-2p\cos20,\\
r^2&=q^2+1-2q\cos26,\\
r^2&=p^2+q^2-2pq\cos46.
\end{aligned}
\]

Equating the first two with the third gives

\[
p^2-q^2-2p\cos20+2q\cos26=0 \tag{1}
\]

and

\[
q^2-2pq\cos46+2p\cos20-1=0. \tag{2}
\]

Adding (1) and (2),

\[
p^2+2q(\cos26-p\cos46)-1=0,
\]

so

\[
q=\frac{1-p^2}{2(\cos26-p\cos46)}. \tag{3}
\]

The interior solution of this system is

\[
p=\frac{\sin34^\circ}{\sin74^\circ},\qquad 
q=\frac{\sin40^\circ}{\sin74^\circ}.
\]

One can verify this directly. Let \(S=\sin74^\circ\). Then

\[
1-p^2=\frac{\sin^2 74^\circ-\sin^2 34^\circ}{S^2}
=\frac{\sin108^\circ\sin40^\circ}{S^2}
=\frac{\sin72^\circ\sin40^\circ}{S^2},
\]

and

\[
\begin{aligned}
2(\cos26^\circ-p\cos46^\circ)
&=\frac{2S\cos26^\circ-2\cos46^\circ\sin34^\circ}{S}\\
&=\frac{\sin100^\circ+\sin48^\circ-\sin80^\circ+\sin12^\circ}{S}\\
&=\frac{\sin48^\circ+\sin12^\circ}{S}\\
&=\frac{\cos18^\circ}{S}=\frac{\sin72^\circ}{S}.
\end{aligned}
\]

Thus (3) gives \(q=\sin40^\circ/S\). Also,

\[
p^2-q^2=\frac{\sin^2 34^\circ-\sin^2 40^\circ}{S^2}
=-\frac{\sin6^\circ}{S},
\]

while

\[
-2p\cos20^\circ+2q\cos26^\circ
=\frac{-2\sin34^\circ\cos20^\circ+2\sin40^\circ\cos26^\circ}{S}
=\frac{\sin6^\circ}{S}.
\]

So (1) holds, and hence (2) holds as well. Therefore the required values of \(p,q\) are as above.

Now in \(\triangle APC\),

\[
\angle PAC=46^\circ+26^\circ=72^\circ.
\]

Compute \(PC\) using the Law of Cosines:

\[
PC^2=p^2+1-2p\cos72^\circ.
\]

Substituting \(p=\sin34^\circ/S\),

\[
PC^2=\frac{S^2+\sin^2 34^\circ-2S\sin34^\circ\cos72^\circ}{S^2}.
\]

Using

\[
S^2-\sin^2 72^\circ=\sin34^\circ\sin2^\circ
\]

and

\[
2S\cos72^\circ=2\sin74^\circ\cos72^\circ
=\sin146^\circ+\sin2^\circ
=\sin34^\circ+\sin2^\circ,
\]

we get

\[
PC^2=\frac{\sin^2 72^\circ}{S^2},
\]

so

\[
PC=\frac{\sin72^\circ}{S}.
\]

Thus in \(\triangle APC\),

\[
AP:PC:AC=\sin34^\circ:\sin72^\circ:\sin74^\circ.
\]

Therefore the angles opposite these sides are \(34^\circ,72^\circ,74^\circ\). Since \(PC\) is opposite the known angle \(72^\circ\), the angle opposite \(AC\) is

\[
\angle APC=74^\circ.
\]

\[
\boxed{74}
\]
